transcription: Main factsheet text only (the CPI program banner and its left navigation, 'SHARE ON:' widget, search box, 'Last Modified Date: June 8, 2023' line, publications footer list and social-media links removed). Section headings (h4) kept as plain lines. The percent-change worked example is a two-column table on the page and is transcribed as pipe-separated lines, one per table row. Inline links flattened to their text; the closing contact line (cpi_info@bls.gov, 202-691-7000) kept as printed. Curly quotation marks around 'cap' and 'floor' and the em dashes kept as printed. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: CPI escalation — six ordered guidelines for writing an escalation agreement (define the base payment, identify the index series with population/area/series/base-period, specify the reference period, state the adjustment frequency, determine the adjustment formula, provide for revisions), CPI-U vs CPI-W compared (over 90 percent vs approximately 30 percent of the U.S. population), why seasonally adjusted data are inappropriate in escalation clauses, and a full worked percent-change example (232.945 minus 229.815 = 3.130; 3.130 / 229.815 = 0.0136; 0.0136 x 100 = 1.4%). Fits step ordering (the guidelines), quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the worked example, a compare table of CPI-U vs CPI-W, and the formula explorer for the percent-change computation.
